# Goldfinger documentation and deployment examples

## Conversation Evidence

> user (turn 4): "We should provide an example fly.toml just so I know how this service could be configured standalone, with the recommended settings for a quick cold start on request to the service."
> user (turn 4): "Our docs should also be clear that this is unsuitable for hosting on a domain which serves a website at the domain apex because the service will be listening there already and we're not building a reverse proxy."
> user (turn 4): "The pattern is to provide one TLD for OIDC (Webfinger and the PocketID app), and it can be the identify provider for another domains services that use custom OIDC."
> user (turn 4): "a separate project combining PocketID, S3 backing and our GHCR container definition will deploy these services together."
> user (turn 5): "I think a good example would include Traefik, PocketID and our Go service"
> user (turn 5): "If it's where the service should be hosted geographically then for now use whatever region definition is within or closest to Australia"
> user (turn 6): "In your Docker Compose example you can use `ghcr.io/arrrgi/goldfinger`"
> user (turn 7): "The Traefik layout should be two-host with `oidc.<domain>`"
> user (turn 12): "The Traefik example can use HTTP-01 challenge"
> user (strategy interview): "Providing the problem definition, answering how Goldfinger solves that and sharing how to use the app in a small set of scenarios in the documentation"

## Goal & Context

Operators and self-hosters need to understand the problem Goldfinger solves, see how to run it, and avoid the one deployment mistake the design makes easy: placing it on an apex that already serves a website. This spec covers the README and two example configurations, a Docker Compose stack and a standalone Fly.io app. Both are illustrations. A separate project combining PocketID, S3 backing, and the published image does the real deployment.

<!-- Source: 60% user / 30% [paraphrase] / 10% [inferred] -->

## Architecture & Data Models

The compose example runs three services on one network. Traefik terminates TLS and routes by host. The apex host goes to Goldfinger and the `oidc.<domain>` host goes to PocketID. PocketID's issuer URL is `https://oidc.<domain>`, which is the value Goldfinger serves. [paraphrase]

## Edge Cases & Constraints

- PocketID's `TRUST_PROXY` setting takes proxy IP addresses or CIDR ranges, not a boolean. The compose network therefore has a fixed subnet so the value is stable. [inferred]
- PocketID requires `ENCRYPTION_KEY` (at least 16 bytes) and accepts `ENCRYPTION_KEY_FILE` for Docker secrets. [inferred]
- Goldfinger's image has no shell, so its compose health check uses the binary's `--healthcheck` flag. [inferred]
- Fly's `suspend` mode is not guaranteed to resume, discards its snapshot on every deploy, and can lose a few log lines. `stop` is the simpler default. [inferred]
- Tailscale requires the WebFinger host to be the domain of the sign-up email. The issuer URL can be a different host. [inferred]

## Acceptance Criteria

- **R1:** The README states the problem, how Goldfinger solves it, the settings reference (flags, variables, defaults), and a small set of usage scenarios: running locally with flags and checking it with `curl`, the compose stack, a standalone Fly app, and several instances on one host. Errors: no error surface beyond the examples in R3 to R5. [paraphrase] [strategy:Documentation]
- **R2:** The README states that Goldfinger cannot share a domain apex with a website, because it listens on the whole origin and does not reverse proxy. It recommends one dedicated domain for OIDC, hosting WebFinger and PocketID, which can act as the identity provider for services on other domains. [paraphrase]
- **R3:** The compose example runs Traefik, PocketID (`ghcr.io/pocket-id/pocket-id`), and Goldfinger (`ghcr.io/arrrgi/goldfinger`). Traefik uses the HTTP-01 challenge, routes the apex host to Goldfinger and `oidc.<domain>` to PocketID, and redirects HTTP to HTTPS. [paraphrase]
- **R4:** In the compose example, PocketID sets `APP_URL`, a `TRUST_PROXY` CIDR that matches the fixed subnet, the encryption key through a secret, and `ANALYTICS_DISABLED`. Goldfinger runs with a read-only filesystem, all capabilities dropped, and `no-new-privileges`, and has a health check. The repository ships only an example environment file with placeholders. [inferred]
- **R5:** A standalone `fly.toml` example uses the GHCR image, sets `ISSUER_URL` and `ISSUER_ADMIN_EMAIL`, listens on the `PORT` Goldfinger uses, forces HTTPS, and sets `primary_region = "syd"`, `auto_stop_machines = "stop"`, `auto_start_machines = true`, `min_machines_running = 0`, a `shared-cpu-1x` machine with `256mb`, and an HTTP check on `/healthz`. Comments show `suspend` and `min_machines_running = 1` as alternatives, with the `suspend` caveats. [paraphrase]
- **R6:** The README explains how to confirm the endpoint before signing up, using Tailscale's WebFinger lookup tool. [inferred]
- **R7:** The compose file passes `docker compose config`, and the image names in the examples match the published image. Errors: a mismatch fails the check. [inferred]

## Boundaries

- This is not the combined PocketID, S3, and GHCR deployment project. The examples are illustrative. [paraphrase]
- No real secrets or real `.env` files in the repository. [inferred]
- The existing `LICENSE` stays as is. [paraphrase]
- DNS-01 certificate challenges, S3 storage, and PocketID administration are out of scope. [inferred]

## Decision Context

The two-host layout fits Tailscale: WebFinger must live on the email domain's host, while the issuer can be anywhere. Path-based routing on one host would also work behind Traefik, but it makes the 404 page unreachable at that host and ties the two routers together. [inferred]

HTTP-01 needs no DNS provider credentials, so the example stays portable. [paraphrase]

Fly region `syd` is the Sydney region. It was chosen as the closest region to Australia. Latency to Tailscale's control plane does not matter because lookups are rare. [paraphrase]

Siblings from the same origin: "Goldfinger WebFinger service" (the settings the docs describe) and "Goldfinger release and quality automation" (the image the examples pull).
